text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz wrapped up Brazil visit in Sao Paulo.
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze flew to Moscow Sunday evening to sign an agreement on Hungarian-Russian cooperation in the fight against organised crime.
- Defence ministers from Italy, Slovenia and Hungary met in Ljubljana on Friday.
- Judges from the International Court of Justice in the Hague ended a two-day visit to the aborted Nagymaros hydroelectric power plant on Friday. (Sat.)
- Socialist representative at the Budapest Local Council Imre Rusznak was attacked by two unidentified assailants and seriously injured outside his home Thursday morning.
- The Alliance of Free Democrats was admitted as a full member on Friday to the Council of European Liberal, Democratic and Reform Parties at its session in Nicosia, Cyprus.

- Gyula Kosa, president of the Agricultural Workers' Advocacy Organisation warned at the weekend that if the majority of farmers are ready to take part in a demonstration they will impose complete blockades on roads and will not withdraw until the cabinet resigns. He also said that one can demonstrate outside Parliament, use an axe to smash down the door and clean out the trash from there.
- The Budapest board of the Young Democrats proposed Saturday that incumbent president Viktor Orban be re-elected at the party's upcoming April 19-20 congress.

- Demonstrators taking part in rallies staged by the Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation and later by the Hungarian Justice and Life Party in Budapest on Friday protested against new tax and social insurance regulations and demanded the resignation of the cabinet. (Sat.)
- GDP grew 1 percent in 1996 calculated at relative prices, reports the Central Statistical Office.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal has informed MPs in writing that the act on conflicts of interest took effect on April 4, and those affected have 30 days to decide whether to give up parliamentary seats or other, irreconcilable posts.
- Foreign companies carry out half of all developments and investments in the telecommunications and trade sector, and 40 percent in other fields, a study reveals.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- In a wide-ranging interview, Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan suggested that an early general election could put an end to a "potentially dangerous political situation". (Sat.)
- Deputy Speaker of Parliament Maria Korodi announced on Friday that the House is to stage a general debate on Monday on a national environmental protection programme. (Sat.)

- Production in the processing industry saw a significant increase along with a drop in employment levels, while exports and imports slightly increased in March, a study by the Hungarian Logistics, Procurement and Reserve Building Association reveals.

- A subordinated loan to be granted to Postabank will not represent a consolidation, said the bank's deputy managing director Robert Muranyi, adding that the bank continues to seek a foreign strategic buyer of a 10-40 percent stake.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has invited a fresh, closed tender for the sale of a 90 percent state-owned stake in the ore mines Recski Ercbanyak Rt.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
